source_quote: Chairperson: Mohamad Al Majzoub
answer: The Management and Marketing Studies Department (DMMS) chairperson is Mohamad Al Majzoub; Assistant Professors are Mohamad Al Majzoub, Maya Daher and Baheej Chaaban.

source_quote: The Management and Marketing Studies Department (MMD) offers three programs –
answer: The Management and Marketing Studies Department offers three programs, Management, Human Resources Management, and Marketing and Advertising, each leading to a BBA.

source_quote: The Human Resources Management program offers students a unique experience in
answer: The HRM program covers the operational and strategic activities of the HR department through an experiential curriculum taught by internationally certified faculty. It requires 99 credits.

source_quote: BHRM 400 HR Development & Training 3 BHRM 300
answer: HRM mandatory courses: BADM 485 Co-op, BADM 490 Entrepreneurship, BHRM 300 Human Resources Management (prereq BMGT 200), BHRM 305 Labor Law & Relations (Junior Standing), BHRM 350 Workforce Planning, Recruitment & Selection, BHRM 400 HR Development & Training, BHRM 450 Performance Management, Compensation & Benefits (all three require BHRM 300), BMGT 205 Organizational Behavior (BMGT 200), BMGT 485 Strategic Management (Senior Standing), and a 3-credit Major Elective.

source_quote: program, students must study 3 credit hours of major electives. Major electives could be
answer: HRM students take 3 credits of major electives, e.g., BITM 415 Business Intelligence, BADM 480 Independent Studies, BFIN 400 Financial Management II, BMGT 300 Project Management, or BMKA 440 Social Media Marketing.

source_quote: prerequisites for co-op training, the program may impose additional conditions.
answer: HRM students complete 8 weeks of Co-op training (BADM 485), usually in the summer of the third year, with faculty follow-up, reports, posters and presentations; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are the essential prerequisites.

source_quote: typically start as an “HR specialist” in one HR function at a large organization or as an
answer: HRM graduates typically start as an HR specialist in a large organization or an HR generalist in a small firm and can advance to upper-level management; others pursue graduate study in management or HRM for academic careers.

source_quote: Demonstrate knowledge of standard HR functions, such as
answer: HRM outcomes: apply business knowledge in decision-making; demonstrate knowledge of HR functions (recruitment, selection, compensation & benefits) per legal requirements and best practices; communicate effectively; analyze business problems; and respond to ethical dilemmas.

source_quote: encompasses 99 credit hours over six semesters and two summer sessions. The first
answer: The HRM BBA spans six semesters and summers (Community Engagement, then Co-op). Year 1 Fall (16 cr): BACC 205, BADM 215, BITM 200, BMGT 200, ENGL 210, MATH 207. Year 1 Spring (16 cr): BACC 255, BADM 225, BADM 235, BADM 250, BMGT 205 Organizational Behavior, ENGL 217.

source_quote: BHRM 305 Labor Law and Labor Relations 3 Junior Standing
answer: HRM Year 2 Fall (18 credits): BADM 230, BECN 301, BFIN 300, BHRM 300, BHRM 305 Labor Law and Labor Relations, and BMKA 200.

source_quote: BHRM 350 Workforce Planning, Recruitment, and 3 BHRM 300
answer: HRM Year 2 Spring (18 credits): BADM 355, BECN 302, BHRM 350, BITM 300, BITM 350, and a Science Elective; then BADM 290 Community Engagement in the Year 2 summer.

source_quote: BHRM 400 HR Training and Development 3 BHRM 300
answer: HRM Year 3 Fall (15 credits): ARAB 212, BADM 420, BHRM 400 HR Training and Development, a 1-credit Community & Sustainability course, a Major Elective, and a Social Science Elective.

source_quote: BMGT 485 Strategic Management 3 Senior Standing
answer: HRM Year 3 Spring (15 credits): BADM 490, BHRM 450, BMGT 485 Strategic Management, a Humanities/Fine Arts Elective, a Social Science Elective; Year 3 Summer: BADM 485 Co-op (1 credit).

source_quote: Resources Management concepts and applications in both small and large
answer: BHRM 300 Human Resources Management, 3(3,0): practical HRM in small and large businesses - recruitment and selection, training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations and legal compliance. Prerequisite: BMGT 200.

source_quote: This course introduces students to the fundamentals of labor law, collective
answer: BHRM 305 Labor Law & Relations, 3(3,0): labor law, collective bargaining, contract administration and Social Security regulations, focusing on Lebanese labor law as applied to HR management. Prerequisite: Junior Standing.

source_quote: particular, this course enables students to conduct effective job analyses, write job
answer: BHRM 350 Workforce Planning, Recruitment & Selection, 3(3,0): workforce planning, job analysis, writing job descriptions, recruiting and modern selection techniques. Prerequisite: BHRM 300.

source_quote: Development function of Human Resources Management. It will enable students to
answer: BHRM 400 HR Training & Development, 3(3,0): designing and implementing training and development plans for current and future organizational needs. Prerequisite: BHRM 300.

source_quote: students how to establish effective performance management processes and design
answer: BHRM 450 Performance Management, Compensation & Benefits, 3(3,0): performance management processes, strategic pay structures, incentives, financial and non-financial benefits, and compensation for executives, expatriates and contingent workers. Prerequisite: BHRM 300.

source_quote: tools to understand and effectively address human behavior in organizations. Special
answer: BMGT 205 Organizational Behavior, 3(3,0): human behavior in organizations - motivation, teamwork, leadership, communication, conflict, negotiation, attitudes, values, personality and perception. Prerequisite: BMGT 200.

source_quote: basic concepts of strategic management, corporate governance and social
answer: BMGT 485 Strategic Management, 3(3,0): an advanced course on strategic management, corporate governance and social responsibility, environmental and industry analysis, internal analysis and strategy formulation in a global context. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: As a continuation of Financial Management I, this course exposes students to the
answer: In the HRM section, BFIN 400 Financial Management II, 3(3,0), is described as firm financial management for value maximization: capital budgeting, capital structure and leverage, dividend policy, mergers & acquisitions, long-term debt and financial planning. Prerequisite: BFIN 300.
review_note: Wording differs from the BFIN 400 description in the Finance and Banking section (p.231), which also covers working capital and ESG.

source_quote: This course covers the skills and concepts necessary to create, manage, market, and
answer: BMKA 450 Events Marketing and Management, 3(3,0): creating, managing, marketing and financing special events, teamwork, and implementing and evaluating an event. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.
